task.description: Implement REQ-191 (service catalog core) per the approved design at lib/letflow/design/req191-service-catalog-core.md: the service_catalog migration (global, unprefixed, with all listed DB-level CHECK constraints including the table-level scope/owner consistency check), the Letflow.ServiceCatalog.Entry Ecto schema, and the Letflow.ServiceCatalog context module (register/2, get_for_tenant/2, list_for_tenant/2, update_scope/2, delete/2), the structural (non-LIKE) referential guard spanning all tenant schemas, a real Lookup implementation for Letflow.Definitions.ServiceScopeValidator.validate/3 built without modifying service_scope_validator.ex, and the explicit resolution of solution_pack.ex's service_catalog_entries hard-fail (retain the hard-fail, update its moduledoc to name REQ-192 as owning follow-up, per design §6). No route or controller file. Confirm with git diff --stat that no router/controller file is touched. Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test and quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: the service_catalog table carries the scope/owner consistency CHECK: an insert with scope 'global' and a non-null owner_tenant_id is rejected by the DATABASE, and so is one with scope 'tenant' and a null owner_tenant_id -- two explicit tests, not changeset-level validation
required_auth and timeout_ms are CHECK constrained at the database level: an insert with required_auth 'BASIC' is rejected, and so is one with timeout_ms 0 and one with timeout_ms 3600001

get_for_tenant/2 returns a global service to any tenant; returns a tenant-scoped service to its owner; and returns NOT FOUND -- not a forbidden error -- for a tenant-scoped service owned by a different tenant, so the two cases are indistinguishable to the caller (three explicit tests)
service_id is globally unique: registering the same service_id for a second, different tenant fails, even when the first is tenant-scoped
register/2 with scope 'tenant' naming a tenant that does not exist is rejected without creating a row

delete/2 of a service referenced by an ACTIVE definition is refused and the error names the referencing definition ids; delete/2 of an unreferenced service succeeds -- and a test confirms the reference check matches an actual SERVICE_TASK service_id attribute rather than a substring of the serialized graph, by registering a service whose id appears only inside an unrelated string in some definition's graph and asserting that definition does NOT block the delete

update_scope/2 narrowing a global service to tenant-scoped is refused, naming the conflicting tenant ids, when another tenant's ACTIVE definition references it; widening a tenant-scoped service to global is always allowed

Letflow.Definitions.ServiceScopeValidator.validate/3 works unchanged when handed a Lookup backed by this catalog: a definition referencing a service not visible to its tenant is rejected at activation, and one referencing a visible service activates -- with no change to service_scope_validator.ex itself, confirmed by git diff

the migration and the module moduledoc both state that this table is GLOBAL rather than per-tenant-schema, give the R-Co-grounded reason (a global-scope entry is referenceable by every tenant and service_id is unique across tenants), and flag the divergence from decision 0003 Decision B for REVIEWER sign-off

solution_pack.ex's service_catalog_entries hard-fail is either made reachable-and-functional or is explicitly retained with the owning follow-up named in this requirement's moduledoc -- it is not left unaddressed, asserted by a test covering whichever outcome was chosen
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
